analysis.investment_thesis: Tenneco India operates an exceptionally capital-efficient business (ROCE 57%, near-zero debt, 90% FCF conversion) but its core products — exhaust systems, catalytic converters, spark plugs — are intrinsically tied to ICE vehicles facing a secular EV headwind. At P/E 42x and P/B 26x, the market is pricing in perpetual excellence that a structurally disrupting industry cannot sustain.
key_strengths: Exceptional capital returns: ROCE 57.3%, ROE 42.6% with virtually zero leverage (D/E 0.02, borrowings only INR 23 Cr).
Strong FCF quality: FCF/Net Income of ~90% (INR 500 Cr FCF vs INR 553 Cr net profit in FY25), positive OCF all 3 years.
Margin expansion despite revenue drop: operating income surged from INR 613 Cr (FY24) to INR 815 Cr (FY25) even as revenue fell ~10.6%, showing real pricing power or cost discipline.
key_risks: EV disruption is existential: catalytic converters, mufflers, exhaust pipes, and spark plugs have no role in electric drivetrains — India's 2W/3W EV push directly targets Tenneco's largest segments.
Revenue already declining: FY25 revenue of INR 4,890 Cr fell 10.6% from FY24's INR 5,468 Cr — this may be the beginning of secular volume decline, not a cyclical blip.

Parent instability: Tenneco Inc. (US parent) filed Chapter 11 in 2022 and is now owned by Apollo Global Management — a PE-owned parent optimizing for exit creates misaligned long-term incentives for the Indian subsidiary.
red_flags: Reserves collapsed from INR 895 Cr (FY23) to INR 514 Cr (FY25) — massive capital extraction via dividends (INR -433 to -686 Cr financing outflows annually) by PE-owned parent, draining the subsidiary.
Revenue contraction in FY25 at a time of strong Indian auto production growth raises questions about market share loss or product mix shift away from ICE vehicles.
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Tenneco India is a genuinely high-quality business by the numbers — ROCE of 57% and near-zero debt would make any investor take notice. FCF conversion at 90% confirms earnings quality, and the FY25 margin expansion (operating income up 33% on revenue down 11%) shows real operating leverage and pricing discipline. These are not the characteristics of a mediocre business.

However, I always invert first. The central question is: will catalytic converters, exhaust systems, and spark plugs matter in 10 years? India's policy direction on EVs — particularly for 2-wheelers and 3-wheelers, which are core Tenneco India segments — points toward increasing headwinds. Meanwhile, the PE-owned US parent (post-bankruptcy Apollo acquisition) is aggressively extracting cash, having drained INR 1,513 Cr in financing outflows over three years while equity shrinks from INR 1,208 Cr to INR 918 Cr. At P/E 42x and P/B 26x, you're paying a premium price for a business with a structurally uncertain future — that is not the Munger way. Hold for those who own it at lower prices, but initiating at current valuations requires far more confidence in the ICE longevity than I possess.
